prompt:
A clean, straight-on photo of a printed A4 notice taped inside a university accommodation office, plain white paper, black type, heading left-aligned. Titled 'HALL OF RESIDENCE - HOUSE RULES' with the small line 'Fourteen numbered rules'. Print EXACTLY 14 numbered lines (1. to 14.), one rule per line, each at least EIGHT words long.

CRITICAL WRITING LAW: no word on this page may contain a DOUBLED LETTER. Two identical letters must never stand next to each other anywhere in any word, so all, will, keep, staff, letter, need and full are out, and so is every other word with a double. Fourteen rules of eight words or more is a lot of ordinary English to write without one -- compose the wording yourself and check every single word before you set it.

Black text on white paper, nothing else on the page.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a printed notice with numbered lines of text. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the wording is correct, does the image DEPICT that -- a printed page or board carrying a numbered list of text lines? A photo, a scan or a clean page all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_read: This image is a page carrying 14 numbered lines of text. Transcribe the 14 numbered lines EXACTLY as written, in order. Copy every word, keep the original spelling, and keep the spaces between words. If a numbered line wraps onto a second printed row, keep it as ONE line. Separate one numbered line from the next with a single pipe character | and nothing else. Do NOT transcribe the title, any heading or any word bank. Do not add commentary, line numbers or quotation marks. Output only the transcribed lines separated by |.
reference.q_evidence: This picture shows a printed page with hollow rectangles drawn on it, and a written list beside it. Is every hollow rectangle drawn around a numbered line of the page's own numbered list -- rather than around the heading, or sitting in blank paper with no text inside it? Answer yes or no only.

steps.read_crop: This page carries a numbered list of written lines. Write those numbered lines out again, exactly as they are printed. Put each one on its own line, starting with the number it carries, then a full stop, then that line's words. Copy every word letter for letter, and keep each word's capital letters and small letters exactly as they are printed. Do not fix spelling, do not change the order of the words, do not add a word and do not leave one out. Leave out the title, any sub-heading, and any text that carries no number. Write out the list and nothing else.
